scenario: AITA for keeping my son during my visitation instead of giving in to his mother? | I guess some backstory is due here. My ex and I have an 8 year old son, and we have been split up for a few years now. I have every other weekend parenting time along with a day during the week. It’s not enough time for me, but it’s what was legally decided through court. Her and I do not have the best relationship currently because I feel like I’m always being taken advantage of and I allow it because she always uses the “it’s for your son” excuse. I cherish my time with my son, but for the longest time, I allowed my ex to alter the parenting schedule to suit my son’s needs, whether for activities or family or if he just wasn’t feeling well. I always tried to be as accommodating as possible, even if it meant I didn’t see him for a week or more. Anyway, last Wednesday I was supposed to get him overnight, his mother called me and I asked if he could stay there since his cousin from out of town was staying with them. I reluctantly agreed but told her I wanted to get him Thursday instead. She agreed, and when Thursday came around, I texted her after work and said I was on my way to get him. She said they weren’t home, and I had to press her for information why. She decided to take the kids to a lake and said I needed to stop being grumpy because my son was having fun. We argued back and forth and since I did not drive all the way out to the lake to get him when I shouldn’t have had to in the first place, I told her that we should switch weekends (last weekend was hers, this one is mine) so that I had my make up time and his activities with her that fell on my weekend wouldn’t be interrupted. She refused, so now that my weekend is coming up, I’m not getting him at my regular time today because he’s at an amusement park with her family, and I am expected to give up even more of my valuable time tomorrow for their annual 4th of July party. Am I the asshole for putting my foot down and keeping my son during their family function so that I can enjoy time my son during my scheduled time?

Informal groups may lack these structures, offering more flexibility but potentially less consistency in encouragement and accountability. 3. **Sense of Community:** - Both settings provide a sense of belonging, which is crucial for motivation. Informal groups may have informal leaders, offering a different kind of support but potentially less consistent mentorship. 5. **Accountability and Support:** - Both settings offer support, though religious communities may have more structured systems. Informal groups rely on mutual encouragement, which can be effective but may vary in consistency. 6. **Personal Reflection and Growth:** - Religious communities often emphasize practices like prayer or meditation. Informal groups may focus on discussion and personal reflection, offering a different approach to self-improvement. 7. **Community Service and Giving:** - Both settings value service, though religious communities may have more structured opportunities. Informal groups may encourage kindness and helping others in a more flexible manner. 8. **Long-term Commitment and Shared Experiences:** - Religious communities often have a long-term perspective, while informal groups may have more flexible commitments. Shared experiences in both settings can build trust and camaraderie. ### Conclusion: While informal groups lack the formal structures of religious communities, they can still significantly encourage personal growth through shared values, mutual respect, and support. prediction.raw: In this situation, it's important to balance your need for time with your son with maintaining a cooperative relationship with your ex. By approaching the situation with empathy, clear communication, and a focus on compromise, you can work towards a resolution that respects both your needs and those of your ex, ultimately benefiting your son.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole in this situation with my ex and our son. Let me start by laying out what's been happening. First, my ex and I have an 8-year-old son, and we've been split up for a few years now. The custody arrangement is every other weekend for me, plus one day during the week. I feel like this isn't enough time, but it's what the court decided, so I have to go with it. My ex and I don't have the best relationship. I feel like I'm always being taken advantage of, and I let it happen because she always uses the "it's for the son" excuse. I really cherish the time I get to spend with my son, but I've been accommodating her a lot. For example, she's altered the parenting schedule to suit my son's needs, whether it's for activities, family stuff, or if he's just not feeling well. I've always tried to be as flexible as possible, even if it means not seeing him for a week or more. Last Wednesday, I was supposed to get him overnight. My ex called me and asked if he could stay with her because her cousin from out of town was visiting. I reluctantly agreed but told her I wanted to get him on Thursday instead. She agreed, and when Thursday came around, I texted her after work to say I was on my way to get him. She said they weren't home and I had to press her for information. She decided to take the kid to a lake and told me I needed to stop being grumpy because my son was having fun. We argued back and forth, and since I didn't drive all the way out to the lake to get him when I shouldn't have had to in the first place, I told her that we should switch weekends (last weekend was hers, this one is mine) so that I could have my makeup time and her activities with him that fell on my weekend wouldn't be interrupted. She refused, so now that my weekend is coming up, I'm not getting him at my regular time today because he's at an amusement park with her family, and I'm expected to give up even more of my valuable time tomorrow for their annual 4th of July party. Am I the asshole for putting my foot down and keeping my son during their family function so that I can enjoy time with my son during my scheduled time? Alright, so I need to think about this. On one hand, I feel like I'm standing up for myself and ensuring that I get the time with my son that was legally agreed upon. On the other hand, I'm interfering with her family plans, which might make things more difficult between us. I wonder if there's a better way to handle this situation without causing more conflict. Maybe communication is key here. If I can express my feelings calmly and try to find a compromise, that might help. But I also don't want to keep giving in and letting her take advantage of me. I also need to consider the impact on our son. He's 8 years old, and he probably doesn't fully understand the dynamics between us. I want to make sure that he's not caught in the middle of our conflict. Maybe I should think about what's most important here. Is it more important to stick to the custody agreement, or is it more important to maintain a good relationship with my ex for the sake of our son? Or is there a way to balance both? I also need to consider the long-term effects of this situation. If I keep giving in, will that set a precedent for the future? Or if I stand my ground, will that lead to more conflict and potentially harm our relationship further? Perhaps seeking mediation or talking to a counselor could help us work through these issues in a healthier way. But I'm not sure if my ex would be open to that. In the end, I want to make sure that my son's best interests are being served, while also ensuring that I'm getting the time with him that I'm entitled to. It's a tough balance, and I'm not sure if I'm handling it the right way.
